answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable stake bound to a unique hardware key. Each agent must lock a bond before it may attest, and that bond cannot forge a second identity because it is tied to one device secret. To flood the network with fake sparrow accounts, an attacker must fund a full bond for every clone, and any delta in duplicated votes gets the whole stake slashed. The cost therefore grows linearly with every fake identity while honest rewards stay fixed, so mass impersonation turns unprofitable.
